name: Toaster
notes: Requires tevila with a brocha. The Teflon-coated rack that contacts food must be immersed.
debates: Rav Moshe Feinstein (Igros Moshe YD 3:24) held a toaster is exempt because bread is already edible before entering, making it a question whether it qualifies as a keili seudah. CRC (Rav Schwartz) rules electrical appliances that would be ruined by immersion are exempt. STAR-K rules tevila without a brocha for Teflon-coated surfaces. Many poskim disagree with Rav Moshe and require tevila with a brocha.

name: Toaster Oven
notes: The rack and tray require tevila with a brocha if food is placed directly on them. The heating element and chamber do not require tevila. If it will break from immersion, ask a Rav.

name: Blender / Mixer
notes: Required even if the cup or bowl is made from an exempt material, because of the metal blades attached to the bottom. Motor/base does not require tevila. For a stand mixer, the brocha may depend on use: with a brocha if used for ready-to-eat food; without a brocha if only for raw dough.
debates: Halachipedia: A mixer used only to mix foods not ready to eat immediately should be immersed without a brocha.

name: Immersion Blender (hand blender)
notes: Metal blades and attachments require tevila with a brocha. Motor handle does not.
tags: blend, stick blender, hand blender, electric

name: Food Processor
notes: Metal blades and glass/metal bowl require tevila. If used only to process foods that are not yet edible (e.g., raw dough), tevila without a brocha. If also used with ready-to-eat foods (e.g., fruits, vegetables), tevila with a brocha.
debates: CRC marks food processor as tevila required, brocha depends on usage: with a brocha if sometimes used with meal-ready food, without a brocha if only for raw food.

name: Coffee Maker (electric, e.g., Mr. Coffee)
notes: Requires tevila if it can withstand immersion. Glass carafe requires tevila with a brocha. If the machine will break from immersion, consult a Rav about alternatives (gift/borrow, or Jewish technician disassembly).
debates: STAR-K: Does not require tevila if it will break if toveled, otherwise requires tevila with a brocha. Kashrut.com: Electric coffee makers (e.g., Mr. Coffee) require tevilah. CRC (Rav Schwartz): Electrical appliances that might be ruined are exempt.

name: Keurig / Pod Machine
notes: According to many poskim, a Keurig does not require tevila because the water passes through a sealed K-Cup and does not contact the metal parts in a way that constitutes a keili seudah. It is preferable to sell to a non-Jew and borrow back.
debates: Halachipedia: According to many poskim does not require tevila. STAR-K: Does not require tevila if it will break; otherwise with a brocha. Preferably sell to a non-Jew and borrow back to avoid the issue.

name: Hot Water Urn (metal, electric)
notes: A metal hot water urn requires tevila with a brocha. After immersion, let the appliance dry thoroughly for at least 48 hours before use. Some recommend using a blow-dryer to speed drying.
debates: STAR-K and most poskim require full immersion with a brocha. CRC (Rav Schwartz) rules electrical appliances that might be ruined are exempt. Halachipedia: If impossible to tovel, one may give it to a non-Jew as a gift on condition that he lend it back.

name: Crockpot / Slow Cooker
notes: Metal or glass insert → tevila with a brocha. Ceramic insert → tevila without a brocha. Glass lid → tevila with a brocha. Outer shell/base → no tevila.

name: George Foreman Grill / Electric Grill
notes: Tevila without a brocha (Teflon-coated metal surfaces). If toveling will break it, consult a Rav.

name: Sandwich Maker / Panini Press
notes: Metal plates that contact food require tevila. Coated surfaces → without a brocha.
debates: STAR-K: Tevila without a brocha (Teflon-coated). CRC: No tevila/no brocha (classified as electrical appliance that may be ruined). Other poskim require tevila.

name: Waffle Maker
notes: Tevila without a brocha because the metal cooking surfaces are Teflon-coated. If toveling will break it, consult a Rav.

name: Air Fryer
notes: The metal basket that holds the food requires tevila (with a brocha if uncoated metal, without if coated). The outer housing is debated — some compare it to a pot cover since steam touches it; others say it's not direct food contact.
debates: AskHalacha.com: The metal basket needs tevila since food goes directly in it. The outer box is more complicated — one can argue it's like a pot cover (requires tevila) or that it doesn't aid cooking directly. Consult a Rav.

name: Instant Pot / Electric Pressure Cooker
notes: The metal inner pot requires tevila with a brocha. The lid (metal with silicone ring) requires tevila with a brocha since steam contacts it. The electric base does not require tevila.

name: Rice Cooker (metal insert)
notes: The metal insert requires tevila with a brocha. If coated with Teflon/non-stick, tevila without a brocha. Electric base does not require tevila.

name: Popcorn Maker (metal)
notes: Tevila with a brocha. If toveling will break it, consult a Rav.

name: Electric Knife
notes: The metal blade requires tevila with a brocha. The motor handle does not.

name: Hot Plate / Platta
notes: Food does not contact the surface directly (pots are placed on it). No tevila required.

name: Warming Tray
notes: Food does not contact the surface directly. No tevila required.

name: Immersion Heater
notes: Does not have direct food contact in the normal sense. No tevila.
debates: Chelkas Yaakov 1:126 and 2:61 relies on the approach that plug-in items are 'attached to the ground' for immersion heaters specifically, though not for electric pots.

name: Microwave Turntable (glass)
notes: If food is placed directly on the turntable → tevila with a brocha. If food is always in a container and never touches the turntable directly → tevila without a brocha.
debates: STAR-K: Tevila without a brocha; with a brocha if food is placed directly on the turntable. Some poskim hold that since it's common to place food directly on it, one should tovel with a brocha.

name: Water Cooler / Dispenser
notes: If completely plastic except for internal metal cooling pipes, debated whether tevila is required. If the metal pipe contacts the water that is dispensed for drinking, many require tevila without a brocha. Consult a Rav.

name: Pot (metal or glass)
notes: Uncoated metal or glass → tevila with a brocha. Teflon/enamel-coated metal → tevila without a brocha.

name: Pot Cover / Lid (metal or glass)
notes: Requires tevila because steam rises and contacts the lid — this is considered direct food contact. Removable lids can be immersed separately.

name: Frying Pan (metal)
notes: Uncoated metal → tevila with a brocha. Teflon/non-stick coated → tevila without a brocha.

name: Teflon-coated Pan
notes: Tevila without a brocha. The Teflon coating on the metal changes the brocha status.

name: Pyrex Cookware
notes: Pyrex is halachically classified as glass. Tevila with a brocha.

name: CorningWare
notes: Comprised mainly of glass/ceramic. Tevila without a brocha.

name: Barbeque Grill (grates/racks)
notes: Racks/grates that contact food directly → tevila with a brocha. Other components (cover, body, wheels) → no tevila. Food-handling tools (tongs, spatula) → tevila with a brocha.

name: Chafing Dish
notes: Food pan → tevila with a brocha. Cover → tevila with a brocha (steam rises to cover — considered food contact). Water pan → no tevila (no direct food contact).

name: Colander / Strainer (metal)
notes: Used with cooked food that is ready to eat. Plastic colander → no tevila.

name: Cooling Rack (metal)
notes: Tevila without a brocha.
debates: STAR-K: Tevila without a brocha. Your original data had 'no tevila' which appears to be incorrect based on the STAR-K chart. The food is already baked (ready to eat) when placed on the rack.

name: Blech
notes: Food does not contact the blech surface directly (pots sit on it).

name: Aluminum Tray (disposable)
notes: Standard disposable aluminum pans designed for one-time use do not require tevila since they are not considered permanent keilim.
debates: Rav Moshe Feinstein (Igros Moshe YD 3:23): Disposable pans that don't last are not keilim and are exempt. STAR-K: Without a brocha if intended for one-time use; with a brocha if intended for multiple uses. CRC: No tevila regardless of how many times used. Mishneh Halachos 7:111 argues aluminum pans are obligated since they could be reused. Thicker/sturdier trays may have a stricter status.

name: Silicone Bakeware
notes: Silicone is not metal or glass. No tevila required.

name: Double Boiler
notes: The food pot (top) requires tevila with a brocha. The water pot (bottom) — if never used directly for food, no tevila; if sometimes used for food, tevila with a brocha.

name: Cutlery: Forks / Knives / Spoons (metal)
notes: Knife used only for arts/crafts → no tevila.
tags: fork, knife, spoon, cutlery, silverware, flatware

name: Corelle Plate / Bowl
notes: Corelle is halachically classified as glass. Tevila with a brocha.

name: China (glazed) / Bone China / Fine Porcelain
notes: Glazed china and bone china → tevila without a brocha.
debates: Ashkenazi poskim generally require tevila without a brocha for glazed china. Sephardi poskim (based on Shulchan Aruch) may hold porcelain does not require tevila at all.
tags: china, porcelain, bone china, dish, plate

name: Cup / Mug
notes: Metal or glass → tevila with a brocha. Glazed ceramic → tevila without a brocha. Plastic → no tevila.

name: Dishes (general)
notes: Metal or glass → with a brocha. Glazed ceramic → without a brocha. Plastic, wood → no tevila.

name: Kiddush Cup (metal or glass)
notes: Does not require tevila if manufactured in Eretz Yisrael by Jews. Requires tevila if manufactured outside Israel or sold through non-Jewish distributors.
debates: STAR-K: Does not require tevila if manufactured in Israel but does require tevila if sold in Israel and manufactured elsewhere. If uncertain about the manufacturer, tevila without a brocha.

name: Kos Shel Eliyahu (Elijah's Cup)
notes: Should be immersed without a brocha.
debates: Halachipedia: One should immerse the Kos Shel Eliyahu used for the Seder night without a beracha.

name: Seder Plate
notes: If food directly touches the plate (metal/glass) → tevila required. If food sits in separate cups/holders and doesn't touch the plate → no tevila.

name: Cake Plate / Tray (metal or glass)
notes: Plate requires tevila with a brocha even if cake is placed on a doily (the doily is considered negligible). Cake plate cover → no tevila.

name: Challah Board
notes: Metal board or glass-top on wood → tevila with a brocha. Plain wood or plastic → no tevila.

name: Sugar Bowl (metal or glass)
notes: If brought to the table → tevila with a brocha. If used only to store sugar and not brought to the table → tevila without a brocha.

name: Salt / Pepper Shaker (metal or glass)
notes: Metal or glass salt cellar/shaker brought to the table requires tevila with a brocha. Metal cap on a plastic body → tevila without a brocha.

name: Candy Dish (metal or glass)
notes: If food contacts the dish → tevila required; the brocha depends on material. If food never contacts the dish → no tevila.

name: Plastic Utensils / Dishes
notes: Common custom is that plastic does not require tevila.
debates: Some authorities argue that similarities between glass and plastic should require tevila. The widespread minhag, however, is to exempt plastic entirely. Some are machmir to tovel without a brocha.

name: Cutting Board (metal or glass)
notes: Plastic or wood cutting board → no tevila (though some who are strict tovel without a brocha will be blessed).

name: Peeler (metal blade)
notes: If used with meal-ready food (e.g., carrots, apples) → tevila with a brocha. If used only with food that requires further cooking (e.g., potatoes only) → tevila without a brocha. Even if handle is plastic, the metal blade determines the requirement.
debates: CRC: With a brocha if sometimes used for meal-ready food; without a brocha if only for foods requiring further cooking.

name: Grater (metal)
notes: If used for ready-to-eat foods (cheese, vegetables) → tevila with a brocha. If only for foods needing further cooking → without a brocha.

name: Cookie Cutter (metal)
notes: If used only with raw, inedible dough → no tevila. If sometimes used to cut ready-to-eat food → tevila without a brocha.
debates: STAR-K (Shach YD 120:11): No tevila if only used with food that is not edible. CRC: Tevila required, without a brocha. The Taz 120:7 disagrees with the Shach; STAR-K follows the Chochmas Adam 73:9 who paskens like the Shach.

name: Scissors / Shears (kitchen, metal)
notes: If used to cut edible/ready-to-eat food → tevila with a brocha. If used only for raw food (e.g., cutting raw meat) → tevila without a brocha.

name: Skewer (metal)
notes: Wood or bamboo skewers → no tevila.

name: Measuring Cup (glass or metal)
notes: Metal or glass measuring cup requires tevila with a brocha. Plastic measuring cup → no tevila.

name: Measuring Spoon (metal)
notes: Tevila without a brocha.
debates: STAR-K (Sefer Tevilas Keilim 11:77): Tevila without a brocha. This may be because it is typically used for measuring raw ingredients rather than serving edible food.

name: Meat Grinder (metal attachments)
notes: If used only for raw meat → tevila without a brocha. If also used for cooked/ready-to-eat food → tevila with a brocha.

name: Ceramic Knife
notes: Tevila without a brocha according to most poskim. Some hold ceramic knives require no tevila at all.
debates: STAR-K: Tevila without a brocha. Some poskim hold ceramics don't require tevila since they are neither metal nor glass.

name: Nutcracker (metal)
notes: If used for nuts brought to the table in their shells → tevila with a brocha. If used for nuts not brought to the table in shells → tevila without a brocha.

name: Peppermill
notes: Tevila without a brocha.

name: Meat Tenderizer (metal hammer)
notes: A wooden hammer with metal on the bottom used for beating meat. Tevila without a brocha, since it is used in the initial stages of food preparation.

name: Bottle (metal or glass, reusable)
notes: If a bottle was purchased filled with food/drink and subsequently emptied by a Jew → generally no tevila required for that bottle.
debates: Rav Moshe (Igros Moshe YD 2:40): A Jew who opens a sealed bottle is considered the one who created the keili, so no tevila. Rav Hershel Schachter: One must pour the contents into another vessel before drinking. Sridei Esh: Have in mind not to acquire the bottle. This dispute applies to all glass bottles bought with drinks (e.g., Snapple).

name: Snapple / Glass Drink Bottle (purchased full)
notes: A famous practical shailah. The question is whether one may drink directly from the glass bottle after opening it.
debates: Rav Moshe Feinstein (Igros Moshe YD 2:40): The Jew who opens the bottle is considered the creator of the keili — no tevila needed, may drink directly. Rav Hershel Schachter: Forbidden to drink from the bottle; pour into another vessel. Sridei Esh (YD 2:29): Have in mind not to acquire the bottle. Chacham Ben-Zion Abba Shaul (Or Litzion OC 1:24): Agrees with Rav Moshe. Rav Menashe Klein (Mishne Halachos 4:107): Permitted since no one intends to acquire a prohibited item.

name: Metal Can (purchased with food)
notes: If bought filled with food and subsequently emptied by a Jew → no tevila. If reusing a metal can for other food → tevila with a brocha. Some poskim permit reuse of a tin can opened by a Jew without tevila.

name: Thermos
notes: Metal or glass thermos → tevila with a brocha. Thermos with a plastic casing and removable metal/glass insert → the insert requires tevila with a brocha; the casing does not. Should preferably be immersed assembled.

name: Washing Cup / Netilas Yadayim Cup (metal)
notes: If used only for netilas yadayim (hand-washing), no tevila is required. It is not a keili seudah.

name: Storage Container (metal or glass)
notes: If used only for storage and never brought to the table → tevila without a brocha. If also used at the table for serving (e.g., a pitcher) → tevila with a brocha.

name: Bread Box (metal)
notes: Storage vessel → tevila without a brocha.

name: Can Opener
notes: No direct food contact. No tevila.

name: Corkscrew
notes: No direct food contact. No tevila.

name: Coffee Grinder (manual)
notes: Requires tevila without a brocha. Coffee is not edible in its ground state, so a brocha is not recited.

name: Flour Sifter
notes: A sifter with a metal net requires tevila without a brocha, even if the frame is made from exempt material. Flour is not ready-to-eat, so a brocha is not recited.

name: Rolling Pin (metal) / Kneading Trough
notes: Metal kneading utensils — rolling pins, kneading troughs — require tevila without a brocha. Used in the initial stages of food preparation, not with ready-to-eat food. Wooden or plastic rolling pins do not require tevila.

name: Brush (grill / pastry / egg yolk)
notes: Brushes are not keilim in the halachic sense. No tevila.

name: Spoon Rest
notes: No direct food contact. No tevila.

name: Trivet
notes: No tevila if food does not contact the surface. Pots are placed on the trivet.

name: Oven Rack
notes: Food does not normally contact the oven rack directly (it sits in pans). No tevila. See toaster oven for different ruling.

name: Knife Sharpener
notes: No food contact. No tevila.

name: Meat Thermometer
notes: Used to measure temperature, not as a food-preparation vessel. No tevila.

name: Dentures
notes: Not considered a keili. No tevila.

name: Medicine Spoon (metal or glass)
notes: If used solely for medicine → tevila without a brocha. If also used for other purposes → tevila with a brocha.

name: Wooden Cask / Barrel
notes: Plain wood → no tevila. If it has metal straps/bands → tevila without a brocha.

name: Pocketknife
notes: Requires tevila if used for food. Should be immersed in the open position so water reaches all areas. If only used for non-food purposes → no tevila.

name: Axe (for carving animals)
notes: Specifically an axe used for carving up the body of an animal. Tevila without a brocha, since it is used in the initial stages of food preparation, not with ready-to-eat food.

name: Baby Bottle
notes: Metal, glass, or Pyrex baby bottles require tevila with a brocha. A bottle used only to heat milk in the bottle (not for drinking directly) does not require tevila.
debates: Some authorities require tevila without a brocha for plastic bottles. Others fully exempt plastic.

name: Baker's Shovel
notes: Tevila without a brocha. Used in the initial stages of baking, not with ready-to-eat food.

name: Bottle Stopper / Cork
notes: Required if made from a material needing tevila and the liquid in the bottle touches the bottom of the stopper. Tevila without a brocha.

name: Butter Dish (metal or glass)
notes: Tevila with a brocha. Food directly contacts the dish.

name: Coffee Percolator (stovetop)
notes: Metal stovetop percolator requires tevila with a brocha. Parts that contact the liquid directly are obligated.

name: Cupboard / Refrigerator Shelves
notes: Storage cupboards, shelves, and drawers do not require tevila, even if food is placed directly on them.
debates: HaGaon Rav Moshe Stern requires tevila for refrigerator drawers, but concludes one should not be forced to change the customary practice of exempting them.

name: Dishwasher
notes: A utensil used for kashering or rinsing out other utensils (hag'alah utensil) does not require tevila. The dishwasher is a cleaning appliance, not a food-use vessel.

name: Dotting Wheel (matzah perforator)
notes: Used for perforating matzoth or dough. Tevila without a brocha, since it is used with food that is not yet edible.

name: Drill (for boring barrels)
notes: Used for boring a hole in a barrel to extract liquid. Does not require tevila.
debates: The Maharil and Yosef Ometz rule tevila is required, but the Shakh rejects their view.

name: Earthenware (coated)
notes: Uncoated earthenware: no tevila. Coated with metal inside & out (functional): tevila with a brocha. Coated both sides (ornamental only) or inside only: tevila without a brocha. Coated only outside: no tevila. Glazed/coated with glass inside & out: tevila without a brocha.

name: Egg Cup (metal or glass)
notes: Used for holding and serving soft-boiled eggs. Food directly contacts the cup. Tevila with a brocha.

name: Egg Cooker
notes: Designated for cooking eggs in their shells. Tevila without a brocha, since the food (egg in shell) does not directly contact the cooking surface in the normal sense.

name: Espresso Machine
notes: Only the parts that come in direct contact with liquid require tevila. The portafilter and brew head require tevila with a brocha; other metal parts that only contact steam may require tevila without a brocha. Consult a Rav.

name: Finjan (metal coffee pot)
notes: A small metal pot used for brewing Turkish-style coffee. Requires tevila with a brocha since food/drink directly contacts the metal.

name: Funnel (metal)
notes: A metal funnel requires tevila with a brocha. A funnel made from wood does not require tevila, even if it has a metal tube.

name: Glass Holder
notes: Holders for glasses do not require tevila, as food does not contact the holder itself.

name: Hag'alah Utensil (kashering vessel)
notes: A utensil used exclusively for kashering or rinsing other utensils does not require tevila, since it is not used for food directly.

name: Ice Cube Tray (metal)
notes: Metal ice cube trays require tevila with a brocha. Plastic ice cube trays do not require tevila.

name: Mortar & Pestle
notes: Metal mortar: if used for spices not otherwise edible without crushing, some rule no brocha; if used for salt or food edible without crushing, a brocha is recited. Wooden or plastic mortar with metal attached: if it functions without the metal, no tevila; if it cannot function without the metal, it is treated as a metal utensil.

name: Needle (for stuffing)
notes: Specifically a needle used for sewing necks and intestines stuffed with flour and oil. Tevila without a brocha.

name: Cooking Net / Wire Basket
notes: A net placed in a kettle to collect limestone: no tevila. A net used for deep frying, steam cooking, or grilling (direct food contact): tevila with a brocha.

name: Oven (food-touching parts)
notes: All parts of the oven that come into direct contact with food require tevila with a brocha: baking trays, grill nets, revolving spit, etc. The oven body itself (which does not touch food directly) does not require tevila.

name: Pail (for soaking meat)
notes: A pail used for soaking meat before or after salting requires tevila without a brocha, since it is used in the initial food-preparation stage, not with ready-to-eat food.

name: Vegetable / Potato Masher
notes: Used for mashing cooked potatoes and other vegetables. Since it contacts ready-to-eat food, tevila with a brocha is required.

name: Refrigerator / Freezer
notes: Even if food is placed directly on the shelves, it is not customary to immerse a refrigerator or its internal shelves. See also Cupboard / Refrigerator Shelves.

name: Saw (for animal butchering)
notes: Used for dissecting the body of an animal. Tevila without a brocha, since it is used in the initial stages of food preparation.

name: Food Scales
notes: The parts of food scales that touch food directly require tevila without a brocha.

name: Knife Sheath / Scabbard
notes: A sheath for storing knives does not require tevila, since food does not contact the sheath.

name: Spatula (metal)
notes: A metal spatula contacts food directly. Tevila with a brocha required.

name: Roasting Spit (metal)
notes: A metal spit used for roasting. Food is impaled directly on it. Tevila with a brocha required.

name: Fruit / Vegetable Squeezer (metal)
notes: A fruit or carrot squeezer. Food contacts the metal directly. Tevila with a brocha required.

name: Steam Utensil (large)
notes: There is a controversy over whether a large steam utensil that is attached to the ground requires tevila. If tevila is required, it is without a brocha. Consult a Rav.

name: Cake Syringe / Decorator
notes: A syringe used for filling or covering cakes with jam or cream. Food contacts the metal directly. Tevila with a brocha required.

name: Metal Table
notes: Some authorities require tevila of a metal table on which food is occasionally placed directly. A wooden table with metal legs, or a metal table on which food is only placed in plates or bowls, is exempt according to all opinions.

name: Taps / Spigots (on barrels)
notes: Taps of barrels require tevila only if the barrel itself requires tevila. Taps of kitchen sinks do not require tevila.

name: Teapot (metal or glass)
notes: A teapot brought to the table requires tevila with a brocha. Liquid directly contacts the metal or glass interior.

name: Tongs (serving / food)
notes: Tongs used for sugar, ice cubes, or serving food. Food contacts the metal directly. Tevila with a brocha required.

name: Metal Tube (purchased with food inside)
notes: When purchasing a metal tube with food already inside, there is no need to extract the food to immerse it before initial use. Once the tube is emptied and reused for food, tevila is required.

name: Water Tank / Solar Boiler
notes: Water tanks and solar boilers do not require tevila.

name: Wicker Utensils
notes: Wicker is a type of wood. Wicker utensils do not require tevila.

name: Ivory Utensils
notes: Ivory utensils do not require tevila.

name: Marble Utensils
notes: Marble utensils do not require tevila.

name: Leather Utensils
notes: Leather utensils do not require tevila.

name: Stone Utensils
notes: Stone utensils do not require tevila.

name: Tablecloth / Napkins
notes: Tablecloths and napkins do not require tevila.

name: Shopping / Food Bags
notes: Bags used to carry food (not for storage) do not require tevila, even if made from a material that normally requires tevila.

name: Shell Utensils
notes: Shell utensils do not require tevila.
